cards.front: seed
cards.back: A small part that can grow into a new plant.
cards.say: seed. A small part that can grow into a new plant.

cards.front: germinate
cards.back: To start to grow. A seed germinates when it gets water and warmth.
cards.say: germinate. To start to grow. A seed germinates when it gets water and warmth.

cards.front: root
cards.back: The part that takes in water from the soil and holds the plant.
cards.say: root. The part that takes in water from the soil and holds the plant.

cards.front: stem
cards.back: The part that holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.
cards.say: stem. The part that holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.

cards.front: leaf
cards.back: The part that catches sunlight and makes food for the plant.
cards.say: leaf. The part that catches sunlight and makes food for the plant.

cards.front: What do plants need to grow well?
cards.back: Water, light, warmth, air and space. They also take in nutrients from the soil.
cards.say: What do plants need to grow well? Water, light, warmth, air and space. They also take in nutrients from the soil.

cards.front: What does a plant take in through its roots?
cards.back: Water and some nutrients from the soil.
cards.say: What does a plant take in through its roots? Water and some nutrients from the soil.

cards.front: What does a plant need from the Sun?
cards.back: Light. A plant uses light to make its food.
cards.say: What does a plant need from the Sun? Light. A plant uses light to make its food.

cards.front: Where does a plant make its food?
cards.back: In its leaves.
cards.say: Where does a plant make its food? In its leaves.

cards.front: Does a plant eat food like we do?
cards.back: No. A plant makes its own food using light, water and air.
cards.say: Does a plant eat food like we do? No. A plant makes its own food using light, water and air.

cards.front: What happens to a plant with no water?
cards.back: It dries out and droops. In the end it can die.
cards.say: What happens to a plant with no water? It dries out and droops. In the end it can die.

cards.front: What happens to a plant kept in the dark?
cards.back: It turns pale and grows weak. It needs light to be healthy.
cards.say: What happens to a plant kept in the dark? It turns pale and grows weak. It needs light to be healthy.

cards.front: What happens to a plant in a very cold place?
cards.back: It may stop growing. Plants need warmth.
cards.say: What happens to a plant in a very cold place? It may stop growing. Plants need warmth.

cards.front: Which part of a plant carries water up?
cards.back: The stem.
cards.say: Which part of a plant carries water up? The stem.

cards.front: Which part of a plant takes in light?
cards.back: The leaves.
cards.say: Which part of a plant takes in light? The leaves.

cards.front: Why do we put pot plants near a window?
cards.back: So they get light.
cards.say: Why do we put pot plants near a window? So they get light.

cards.front: Why do we water plants?
cards.back: Plants need water to grow and stay healthy.
cards.say: Why do we water plants? Plants need water to grow and stay healthy.

cards.front: Why do plants need space?
cards.back: So their roots and leaves can spread out and get light and water.
cards.say: Why do plants need space? So their roots and leaves can spread out and get light and water.

cards.front: What colour are healthy leaves?
cards.back: Green.
cards.say: What colour are healthy leaves? Green.

cards.front: What do seeds need to start growing?
cards.back: Water and warmth. Most seeds also need air.
cards.say: What do seeds need to start growing? Water and warmth. Most seeds also need air.

cards.front: What part grows down from a seed first?
cards.back: The root.
cards.say: What part grows down from a seed first? The root.
